Saturday
Football
8am (all times GMT)Matchday live
Wake up to the weekend’s action with our unbeatable rolling news and buildup blog. Simon Burnton and Tom Bassam are our early risers on a day featuring three Premier League games, plus a full programme of Scottish Premiership, Championship and League One and Two fixtures. Other than a bacon/vegan bap and a hot cuppa, there’s no better way to start your footballing Saturday. Join the conversation by emailing matchday.live@theguardian.com
Nations Championship
1.10pmWales v Japan live
Steve Tandy’s side end their 2026 programme on finals weekend against Japan at Twickenham and, after a torrid run of just two wins in 27 Tests between October 2023 and March 2026, Wales have the opportunity to record a fifth win this calendar year. They have beaten Italy, Fiji and Japan and, to national celebrations, New Zealand for a first victory over the All Blacks since 1953. It is a far healthier picture than a year ago when Tandy was just a few months into the role of head coach, and Wales ended 2025 with a record 73-0 thumping at home to South Africa. Blog host Lee Calvert is all set to feast on more bread from rugby heaven.
Premier League
3pmClockwatch
Rob Smyth buckles up for the two mid-afternoon matches, with Manchester United’s clash with Brentford front and centre. New head coach Mauricio Pochettino is in no doubt about the scale of the job at Old Trafford as United chase just their second league win of the season against the west Londoners. His hapless, error-prone side are leaky at the back and short of confidence as they face the growing nightmare of a Premier League relegation battle. Then there’s Leeds v Coventry, with the Yorkshire club riding high in seventh place and last week’s impressive 4-1 win at Chelsea leaving some fans debating whether they could qualify for Europe in their second season back in the top flight.
Nations Championship
4.40pmEngland v New Zealand live
Lee Calvert is back on deck for minute-by-minute coverage as England aim to inflict more misery on a shaken New Zealand a week after claiming a record 37-12 victory over the All Blacks. Steve Borthwick’s side missed out on a place in the final by a single point, but there is still third place to play for, as well as a slice of history. No Red Rose side has defeated the All Blacks three times in a row; a sixth defeat this year for the All Blacks would signal their worst annual campaign since 1949. Robert Kitson, Andy Bull, Michael Aylwin and Gerard Meagher are our reporting team at the Allianz Stadium.
Premier League 
5.30pmIpswich v Aston Villa live
Unai Emery’s Villa lost 1-0 to Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday and are on a run of three straight draws in the league. Their last win came against Manchester City a month ago as their overhauled squad takes time to settle. Their Portman Road hosts are struggling of late too. After a bright start to life in the top tier, Gary O’Neil’s side have garnered just two points from the past five games. Scott Murray is the blog host.
Formula One
6pmQatar Grand Prix qualifying live
Philip Cornwall is on call for spats and spins as the season winds to a close. With fractious foes Max Verstappen and George Russell revving up their long-running feud and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc clashing on track there’s still plenty of entertainment left in the old circus. Verstappen has won four of the past six races and is now looking a safe bet for overall runner-up, denying Mercedes the Antonelli-Russell one-two they had hoped for. The divisive Dutchman has also won the last three times in Qatar and is going for four in succession from five editions. Russell, who started the season as title favourite, is now fourth but level on points with McLaren’s fifth-placed Lando Norris, who has been first and second in the last two rounds. Giles Richards reports.
Sunday
Football
8amMatchday live
A compelling day of Premier League action – six games in total – culminates with the weekend’s crackerjack billing as title pacesetters Arsenal face their old nemesis Manchester City. Before that blockbuster there’s the Merseyside derby at lunchtime, followed by Brighton v Newcastle, Crystal Palace v Hull, Fulham v Bournemouth and Sunderland v Tottenham. Join Dominic Booth for breaking news and all the vibes from around the grounds by emailing matchday.live@theguardian.com. 
T20 international cricket
8.15amAustralia v England live
Megan Maurice has over-by-over coverage of the fourth T20 between the old Ashes rivals. On Friday, England all-rounder Jamie Overton claimed a maiden five-wicket haul in international cricket as the tourists secured a seven-wicket victory under the DLS method at the Gabba to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series. Sydney is next up, before the concluding meeting in Canberra on Wednesday. Ali Martin reports. 
Premier League
12pmEverton v Liverpool live
Liverpool are in fourth place with 21 points from their 11 games, seven points behind Arsenal, but there are signs that Andoni Iraola is beginning to make them tick. Last week’s 4-0 hammering of a woeful Manchester United followed an away win ‌at Crystal Palace with Florian Wirtz scoring in both games, signs that the German is starting to make the impact expected when he signed from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025. It is Iraola’s first Merseyside derby against the hosts who are reeling from a 4-0 shellacking by Brentford and have a dismal record against their city rivals: just two wins in their last 31 top-flight meetings with Liverpool. Daniel Harris live blogs the derby with Andy Hunter our big-game reporter. 
Nations Championship 
1.10pmScotland v Argentina live
Scotland are back to full strength for Sunday’s Nations Championship seventh-place playoff clash against Argentina at Twickenham, with coach Gregor Townsend making 11 changes to the starting lineup. They will hope to finish with a victory after four wins and only two losses to South Africa and the All Blacks, having run in 11 tries to defeat Japan 67–5 at Murrayfield last weekend. When the teams last met back in July, Scotland claimed a 47–38 victory in Córdoba. Daniel Gallan blogs the Test, with Luke McLaughlin reporting from Twickenham. 
Premier League 
2.05pmClockwatch
Michael Butler and Dominic Booth are our dynamic duo for all the Premier League crash, bang, wallop. Brighton meet Newcastle, Crystal Palace host Hull, Fulham face Bournemouth and – perhaps the pick of the bunch – Tottenham travel to Sunderland. Spurs are showing signs of life at last under Roberto De Zerbi, winning four of their last five league matches – that’s more than in their first 26 games in 2026 combined. Sunderland, meanwhile, have climbed off the foot of the table after avoiding defeat in their last two games.
Formula One
4pmQatar Grand Prix live
Michael Butler is in the driving seat for the Qatar grand prix, the scene of the 2024 war of words where George Russell accused Max Verstappen of bullying and Verstappen said he “lost all respect” for his Mercedes rival. That playground antipathy has escalated of late, so a return to actual racing will provide some welcome relief for those seeking actions over words. Giles Richards reports. 
Nations Championship final
4.40pmFrance v South Africa live
Daniel Gallan returns for the Nations Championship inaugural climax. Sunday’s match ‌is a repeat of their meeting at the Stade de France a fortnight ago when France edged the ‌Springboks in a 21-19 thriller, the first of successive defeats for the world champions who also lost to Ireland in Dublin last weekend. Robert Kitson, Andy Bull and Gerard Meagher report from the Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.
Premier League
4.30pmArsenal v Manchester City live
City, already six points behind the Gunners, travel to the Emirates low on confidence after taking a single point from their past four league matches. Despite their impressive results, Arsenal are showing a worrying inability to kill off opponents, however. In their past nine matches in all competitions, Arsenal have won just one game by more than a single goal. They logged 30 shots in their midweek 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund but just four of those were on target. Kai Havertz has a paltry three Premier League goals this season while fellow forward Viktor Gyokeres has yet to get off the mark in the top flight. Having been the crux fixture in recent seasons, there’s a different vibe around Sunday’s meeting. Rob Smyth helms the blog with David Hytner, Barney Ronay and Ed Aarons reporting.
American football
6pmNFL live
Graham Searles keeps pace with the nine Sunday evening clashes as week 12 unfurls yet more plot lines on Thanksgiving weekend. Kirk Cousins, released by the Falcons last offseason, returns to the US Bank Stadium for his first game since rejoining the Vikings. After defeat by San Francisco last week, there’s more pressure weighing on Cousins against Atlanta. Elsewhere, there’s a critical NFC West showdown between Seattle and the 49ers. Only an Eddy Pineiro field goal for San Francisco at the two-minute warning separated the sides when they last met. Welcome to the festive fun.

סוף השבוע מביא עמו שפע של אירועי ספורט מרכזיים ברחבי העולם, הכוללים משחקי כדורגל בפרמייר ליג, טורנירי ראגבי ומרוצי פורמולה 1. במוקד משחקי הכדורגל עומד דרבי המרסיסייד המסורתי בין אברטון לליברפול, לצד התמודדויות מרכזיות נוספות כמו המשחק של מנצ'סטר יונייטד והמפגש בין ארסנל למנצ'סטר סיטי.

בזירת הראגבי, גמר אליפות האומות מספק קרבות מסקרנים בין נבחרות מובילות כמו ויילס ואנגליה מול יריבותיהן. במקביל, עולם המנועים מתמקד במוקדמות הגרנד פרי בקטאר במסגרת עונת הפורמולה 1, כאשר הנהגים המובילים נאבקים על מיקומם הסופי בטבלה רגע לפני סיום העונה הנוכחית.
